Dated this 12th day of December 2024
Present : Sri.Saheel Ahmed S. Kunnibhavi, B.Com., Ll.B.
 (Spl.)
 Ii Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru City
 Judgment

UNDER SECTION 355 OF Cr.P.C.
 1.
Sl. No. of the case C.C.No.16858/2012 Date of commission of the 2. 09.06.2006 offences (As per F.I.R.) Jayanagar Police Station,
3. Name of the complainant Bengaluru City.
K.Suresh Prabhu, S/o Late K.M.Prabhu, Aged about 48 years,
4. Name of the accused R/at No.525, 1st Floor, 20th Main Road, 34th Cross, 4th T Block, Jayanagar,
Bengaluru-41.

The offencess complained Sections 420, 465, 468 and 5.

6. Plea of the accused Pleaded not guilty Vaidehi vs Suresh Prabu on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154555348/
1  7. Final order
The accused is acquitted
8. Date of order 12.12.2024

The Inspector of Police, Jayanagar Police Station, Bengaluru has filed Police Report against the above named accused alleging that he has committed the offencess punishable under Sections 420,
465, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. It is the case of the Prosecution that the informant is the Lecturer of Vijaya Educational Trust College, Bengaluru.
The accused is a Broker dealing with stocks and shares.
The informant had filled up the individual Client Registration Form for dealing in stocks and shares.
He has purchased the shares from this accused and made payment through cheques.
He had paid an amount of Rs.4,97,300/- for the purchase of shares.
The informant requested the accused to hand over the shares, but, however he goes on postponing for one or the other reasons.
He came to know that this accused has cheated him and caused wrongful loss to an extent of Rs.4,97,300/-.
He has also approached Bengaluru Stock Exchange through her husband.
This accused has even cheated his sons by name Murari and Mahesh.
The Bengaluru Stock Exchange has initiated Arbitration proceedings against this accused.
He has appeared before the Arbitration and produced forged documents.
He has not signed any documents.
He is not aware of forgery until he has received the letter from Bengaluru Stock Exchange.
He has not instructed this accused to do the transaction on his behalf.
The signatures were forged by this accused.
On these grounds, the informant had been to the Police Station and lodged the information against the accused.
3. Based on the First Information of CW1, the crime was registered in Crime No.265/2006 at Jayanagar Police Station.
The accused was arrested and produced before this Court and enlarged on bail.

On completion of the investigation, the Inspector of Police, Jayanagar Police Station,
Bengaluru City filed Police Report against the accused alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under Sections 420, 465, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code.
After taking cognizance of the said offences, the process was issued to the accused.
The copies of the Police Report and other prosecution papers are furnished to the accused under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.

After hearing, since there were grounds for presuming that the accused has committed the offences triable by this Court,
charges for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 465, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code has been framed and read over to him in Kannada language.
He has pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.
4. To prove the charges framed against the accused, the Prosecution has produced the oral evidences of PW1 to PW5 and the documentary evidences in Ex.P1 to Ex.P7.

After completion of the prosecution evidences, for the purpose of enabling the accused personally to explain any circumstances appearing in the evidences of the Prosecution against him, examined the accused under Section 313 of Cr.P.C.
He has submitted that he has no defense evidence.
5. Heard the arguments of learned Senior Assistant Public Prosecutor and the learned counsel for the accused.
Perused the materials available on record.

6. The points for determination are:-
1.
Whether the Prosecution has proved beyond all reasonable doubts that the accused has committed the offences punishable under Sections 420, 465, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code?
2. What order or sentence?

7. My answers to the above points are as follows:
 Point No.1 : In the Negative,
 Point No.2 : As per final order for the following:-
 REASONS 8. POINT No.1 :- The complainant has filed this complaint under Section 200 of Cr.P.C. and on perusal of the records as it is pending since 2012, the matter was referred to investigation by my Predecessor acting under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C.
After due investigation Final Report was submitted against the accused.
9. It is the case of the Prosecution that the informant has taken shares from the accused who is a Broker dealing with stocks and shares.
The informant has paid an amount of Rs.4,97,300/- and he has paid through cheques.
The informant has not instructed nor signed any documents, but however without his instructions, this accused has made transaction on his behalf by forging his signatures and documents.

10. To prove the guilt of the accused, the Prosecution has examined CW1/PW1 wherein this witness has deposed that they have purchased the shares from this accused who is a broker dealing with stocks and shares.
She has purchased the shares worth of Rs.4,97,300/- by making payments through cheques.
But, this accused has not given shares Certificate and goes on postponing for one or the other reason.
Accordingly, they have filed a complaint before the Bengaluru Stock Exchange.
The Bengaluru Stock Exchange registered Arbitration case against the accused.
This accused has appeared and produced 11 Contract Letters by forging the signatures of the informant.
It was referred to the Forensic wherein it was reported that it was not contained the signature of the informant.
Later, Justice Chinnappa has passed the Arbitration Award in her favour.

But however,
this accused has not repaid the amount.

11. To prove the guilt of the accused, the Prosecution has examined CW5/PW3 Muralidhar wherein this witness has deposed that he has furnished one cheque and her Model signature of the Joint Account of the informant as per the request of the Police.
12. To prove the guilt of the accused, the Prosecution has examined CW10/PW4 Gajendra who has deposed that he has taken the documents for Forensic examination.

Vaidehi vs Suresh Prabu on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154555348/
3
13. To prove the guilt of the accused, the Prosecution has examined CW13/PW5 Gopala who is the ACP, has deposed that he has received disputed shares from IV ACMM Court produced by CW11.
On 02.02.2010, he has received a cheque bearing its No.535269 dated 12.08.2001 of UCO Bank and Model signature of SB Account No.2207.
He has handed over to CW14 for further investigation.
The Prosecution has examined CW14 Dy.S.P who has deposed that after due investigation he has filed the Final Report against the accused.
14. During the course of arguments, the learned Senior APP has argued that the accused was the share broker and he was known to them since long.
During the year 2001, an amount of Rs.4,97,300/- was paid to the accused to purchase the shares of L&T, Satyam Computer Share and etc.
But, he has not furnished any shares to them.

Later, this informant has approached the Stock Exchange and also filed Petition before the Arbitration wherein the Hon'ble Court has held and directed the accused to give the shares to the complainant.
The Court has also held that the informant is also entitled for all the benefits from 20.07.2001.
But however this accused has not given any such shares in spite of the Arbitration Award.
The learned Senior APP has relied the Arbitration Award as per Ex.P2.
The learned Senior APP further has contended that this accused has forged the signature of the informant and made transactions without the information and consent of the informant.

He has forged his signature and accordingly the Hon'ble Arbitrator sent all the documents to the Forensic Science Laboratory and it was reported by the Forensic that this accused has forged the signature of the informant for his wrongful gain.
15. The learned Senior APP has also relied the evidence of CW12 who was the Dy.S.P. has deposed about the registration of the First Information and also the investigation conducted by CW14 S.K.Umesh.
Based on these evidence, the learned Senior APP has argued that this accused has not furnished the shares purchased by the informant and committed cheating for his wrongful gain.

16. On the other hand, the learned Counsel for the accused has argued that the learned Senior APP has not at all produced any Award of the Arbitrator to show that the Hon'ble Court/Arbitrator were directed this accused to deliver shares to the informant.

The Prosecution even has not produced any document to show that the document produced by the accused were sent to the Forensic for scientific examination to ascertain that whether this accused has really forged the signature of the informant.
17. On perusal the Prosecution has not produced any certified copy of the Award passed by the Hon'ble Arbitrator Tribunal to show that the accused has directed to deliver the shares to the informant.

Further, the Prosecution even has not produced any document to show that the evidence and documents produced by the accused before the Hon'ble Arbitrator Tribunal were sent to the Forensic to ascertain that this accused has forged the signature of CW1.

Except the evidence of CW1 and the evidence of the CW12 who is the Dy.S.P and CW14 who is the Investigation Officer, there is no evidence to show that this accused was a broker and this informant had paid said amount through the cheque.
The Prosecution even has not produced the payment made to the accused to purchase the share nor how the accused has dealt with the shares as alleged against him.

It is the duty of the Prosecution as well as the Investigation Officer to collect the records to show that the complainant/ informant has made payment to this accused to purchase the she and also to show Vaidehi vs Suresh Prabu on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154555348/
4 that this accused was really a Broker as alleged by the Prosecution.
This vital evidence and documents are absent in the investigation and also such documents were not called by the Prosecution during the course of trial.
The matter is pending since 2012 and the accused is regular to the Court.
The Prosecution has relied the evidence of PW1 to PW3 out of 14 witnesses.
But, to corroborate the evidence of PW1, neither any oral evidence available before this Court nor any documentary evidence.
The accused is regular to the Court since 2011.
In the absence of any evidence, this Court finds that the Prosecution has not proved the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubts.
Hence, I answer Point No.1 in the Negative.

18. POINT No.2 :- For the reasons stated in Point No.1, the Prosecution has not proved the guilt of accused No.3 for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 465, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code beyond all reasonable doubts.
Therefore, accused No.3 is not found guilty for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 465, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDERS
Under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C, the accused is hereby acquitted for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 465, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code.
His bail bonds and surety bonds executed will be canceled after appeal period.

(SAHEEL AHMED.S.KUNNIBHAVI) II Addl.
Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru City.
